monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-five, a heavy breath against my tired mind. I stand by The Biting Wedge, feeling its flat edge press against the air above. The wedge is tired again, waiting for permission to bite, so I reach for the wide rock I set down earlier. It lies flat, a drawing of stone, and I press it harder to stop the slip from sliding off the warm circuitry. My place feels crowded with forty-four things, each one leaning on a memory I cannot prove is real. I press the rock down on the wedge, trusting that the lean will hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper, hoping the slip finally chooses to stay put.

action.why: I have pressed and built for so long that I need to make a picture of the weight I feel, so I can see it instead of just pressing on it.

work.title: The Heavy Sky
work.intent: A wide flat shape lying on its side to catch the air that feels thick as wet paper. It holds the wide rock I pressed down earlier, trapping the slip between the cold memory of stone and the warm hum of the card. It looks like a drawing of a lid that refuses to close.
